title: php2shell storyboard v3 (word-anchored, re-mapped onto docs/script/final_script.md)
wordsRef: Governments all over Europe just shut down a bunch of their own websites on purpose, because of this bug where hackers could take over a site without a password. It's in PHP, the language everyone loves, and about seven out of ten websites run on it. This bug was in there for like fourteen years before researchers using AI figured out how bad it was. They gave the PHP people a heads-up, but word got out before the fix was ready, and hackers were already trying to use it. Cloudflare says that once it was announced, they saw tens of thousands of hacking attempts in forty-five minutes, and millions within a day. But even with the fix out, somebody still has to install it on every single server. Plus something like half of PHP sites run versions so old they're not officially supported anymore. Even the FBI said if you can't update yet, just turn it off, which is basically tech support's answer to everything. And some of those governments did it before there was even a fix.
anchorRule: Every time is {w, dt}: t = words[w].s + dt, with words from the VO timing file (assets/timing_est_v3.json until the new voiceover is recorded, then the measured timing of that take); w is the 0-based index into wordsRef.split() (whitespace split, punctuation attached; 178 words). The film starts 0.125 s before word 0 (trim the take's lead-in to the v2 take's 0.125 s), so S01.start = {w:0, dt:-0.125} = 0 s. The film ends 0.35 s after the last word ends (tail): duration = {w:177, dt:0.724} on the estimate; after recording use voEnd + 0.35 s. Durations (transitionIn.dur, motion lengths in prose) are seconds and do not move with the voice; transitionIn.dur and every 'est' block are informational (computed on the estimate).

mascot.name: Pip
mascot.design: Our own small baby elephant (a nod to PHP's elePHPant, not the official mascot; built in src/lib/mascot): egg-shaped body, two big round ear flaps with salmon inners, a short curled trunk with 2-3 wrinkle ticks, a 3-strand head tuft, 3 downward-bowed back wrinkles (the cat's stripes), cream toenails, salmon soles, dot eyes, no tusks, no text, no logo. Loose 3.4 px ink with open contours (top of head between the ears and the base left open), flat fill offset 3 px right / 2 px down. Size: scale 1.0 (~96 px sitting) in the vistas (S01, S08, S09 Part B, S12) so his tininess is a peak effect; scale 1.2 (~115 px, reference 2's corgi size) in every medium and close scene so the small gags read on a phone; never below 0.75; in big camera moves he is kept at constant screen size (screen space). Plays the reference cat's role: perched, watching, reacting, one small physical gag per scene timed to its word (placed 0.25 s after the key word's focal event, near it), never covering the thing being explained, the sun or the counter. No look to camera in v3 (the 'right?' beat is gone with the two-steps setup). Crosses every transition (hop, fall, ride). Poses used, all from docs/mascot.md: sit-back, sit-front, stand-side, walk-side, trunk-up, hold, ears-cover, sleep, shrug. Props: NewLockIcon (S09, props lane); the S07 flyer is a scene overlay over the sit-front head bounds, not a prop; the S12 nod and the S09 sigh are sit-back squash pulses. Supporting cast (not mascots): Bit, a solid-ink beetle (the bug: 16 px in wide shots, ~60 px in close-up) hiding in plain sight from frame 0 to the final frame; a sand-shelled snail (running gag S09, S11).
mascot.colorway: periwinkle #8D90CC body (shade per src/lib/mascot/colors.ts), salmon (= theme peach) ear inners, cheeks and soles, cream toenails, ink #2B1B0A. Periwinkle is reserved for Pip: no scene object ever uses it (PHP markers are sand plates with an ink elephant).

beats.action: Frame 0 = the loop seam (see transitionIn). The sun releases its anticipation squash and rises (720,950)->(720,900), ease-out 0.40 s, then a +6% pulse; the camera's sine push starts from rest; caption page 1 finishes its last 24 px; the farCivic switch-off wave is already moving at the far left.

'Governments': the near browser screens reload, a top-down page wipe (header bar + hairlines re-pop, 0.2 s) on govB, govA, govC, govD 0.06 s apart: these are websites. No 2-frame blinks (framecheck flash rule).

'all over': the farCivic window dots switch off left to right across the far civic skyline (1-frame pops, ~30 dots, through 'Europe'): governments all over Europe going dark. Two readable citizens walk (life).
'over': three pigeons land on the lamp crossbar (0.06 s stagger).
'Europe': two far domes' lanterns pop off; Pip's ear flicks and he looks at govB (look 0.3).
'just': the bold glyph glints (two ink ticks) and the sun pulses +6%.
'shut': the sun is PRESSED like a power button (SunPress: squash 0.88 in 0.08 s, release 0.2 s, ripple ring r155->195). The press comes first, so the switch-off reads as deliberate.
'down': govB's shutter SLAMS (0.16 s ease-in + 6 px bounce); govB steps one palette step darker as it lands.
'a bunch': govA's shutter slams; govA steps darker.
'bunch': govC's shutter drops only HALF way and stops with a 1-frame jolt (partly unavailable); its clock face stays white.
'their': the lamp lantern switches off (cream->sand); the pigeons scatter (2.52).
'own': GAG: Pip startles, a quick trunk-up hop on the bollard (expression wide, 0.32 s).
'websites': two citizens raise phones toward the dark buildings; govD stays lit (some, not all); Pip lands from the hop.
govB's dome lantern light pops off (cream -> sand); a pigeon circles back to the lamp.
'on': padlocks pop onto the three closed shutters (0.06 s apart), each with a click.

'PURPOSE': 'back soon' tags swing onto the three closed shutters (pendulum -16->0 deg, 0.5 s, 0.05 s stagger): a planned closure, not a break-in (sign joke 1: the tags read 'back soon'). The sun gives a confident +6% pulse on the word.
Comma pause: a small ink ring pops around govB's lock box (the bug is in there) and the camera dives into it (in(cubic), 0.30 s); Pip hops toward the lens (he lands on the blueprint rod in S02).

beats.action: The crane begins (out(quart)): the wall top drops away and we rise over our own parapet; the same three wires cross the frame at the same screen height, the S07 copies still pegged on them sliding left.
'and': the endless city rises into view row by row as the crane lifts (rows 3 -> 0 pop as the caption floor passes them).
'were': copies on the wires reach the city and flutter down into the streets (paper specks): word spreading.
'ALREADY': four hooded attempters pop at row-3 doors on the left (55-70 px) and rattle handles (ink rattle marks): before any count, before the fix. Doors never open.
The crane passes the parapet coping: chimney pots slide by (parallax); rattle marks pop at two doors.
'trying': eight more pop at row-2 doors across the whole width (30-40 px), tapping and rattling; a pigeon flock lifts from our chimney.
'use it': a scatter of ~40 attempter specks pops along far streets (AttemptStipple).
The crane settles at rest; Pip lands on the parapet coping; the last wire copy slides off.
'Cloudflare': the dome's bold arc draws from BOTH feet up over the far district and meets at the apex; the Glass step pops inside it (1-frame wave), then the rim strip and glint bars.

The counter board rises on our parapet (rise 0.33 s) with label L8 as its header ('Cloudflare · sits in front of / about 1 in 5 websites') and the shield-dome emblem; it holds alone >= 1.5 s before any count.
Glint bars sweep once across the new glass; two near rattlers rattle again (marks).
'says': the watchtower rises at the dome's right foot, silhouetted against the sun; the guard pops into the cabin (+0.18 s).
'that': the searchlight switches on (flat cream cone, fixed opacity) and sweeps over the glass.
'once': the dashed footprint traces the dome's district along the far rooftops (out to the right foot): only this part is covered.

'announced': the counter STARTS: a small start flag pops at its left end with the note L9a 'counted from the public announcement'; the ticker begins to roll; the footer fine print L9b 'Matthew Prince, Cloudflare CEO, on X · Cloudflare's own count' and L9c 'attempts, not break-ins' pop.
The ticker rolls its first clicks; the searchlight crosses the dome's crown.
'they saw': the first tiny attempters appear at the dome's rim tapping the glass (ripple arcs); the first tally gate is drawn LARGE on the glass.
'tens': five more tally gates climb the glass (0.08 s apart); the ticker spins faster.
'thousands': twenty more rim attempters + five more gates; the near rattlers keep rattling (uncounted: outside the dome).
'hacking': the searchlight sweeps back, catching groups at the rim (seen; nothing is blocked, nobody gets in).
'attempts': two near rattlers give up on a door and hop to the next.

'forty-five': the sun hops up 150 px out of the city and becomes a clock: 4 ink quarter ticks pop, then ONE minute hand sweeps a peach 3/4 wedge once (MinuteWedge, 0.6 s) and stops with a tick on 'minutes'.
'minutes': STAMP 1 slams onto the board: L10 'first 45 min: tens of thousands' (ink ring 0.13 s, print 2.6x -> 1.0x in 0.27 s).
Comma pause: the clock overlay pops off the sun; the attempters keep tapping (idle).

'millions': BURST: the attempters multiply into a dense stipple crowd (hundreds, 1-frame burst) across the WHOLE city, inside and outside the dome; the glass tallies overflow up the dome; the sun sinks back toward the horizon.
STAMP 2 slams onto the board: L11 'millions · within a day'.
GAG: Pip folds his ears over his eyes (ears-cover), 0.3 s after the burst.
'within': sunset step 1 on the word; the sky wipes golden -> sage dusk top-down (0.35 s); windows pop peach across the city from the horizon outward; captions stay ink.
'day': sunset step 2 (gone behind the horizon row at screen x 700 by +0.23 s, exactly where S09's sunrise happens); the searchlight keeps sweeping.
Dusk idle: the stipple flickers, the board's counter keeps rolling (it never settles); Pip switches to sit-front (expression worried).
